Path signatures are collections of iterated integrals along paths.
Signatures are invariant under time re-parameterization.
Signatures encode the path up to tree-like excursions.
Linear functionals of the signature form an algebra on path space.
Signatures are universal approximators for continuous functionals on compact sets of rough paths.
The dimension of the truncated signature grows as 1 + d + ... + dm for a d-dimensional path truncated at degree m.
Model order reduction (MOR) techniques are applied to signature-based models to reduce complexity.
MOR for signatures is adapted from methods used in deterministic control systems.
The reduced signature equation is introduced in Section 3.3 of the paper.
Numerical examples include applications to the (rough) Bergomi model in finance.
For the classical Bergomi model, a reduced dimension of 5 achieves a relative error of order 10⁻² in implied volatility.
For the classical Bergomi model, a reduced dimension of 11 achieves a relative error of 10⁻⁴.
For the classical Bergomi model, a reduced dimension of 27 is exact up to machine precision.
For the rough Bergomi model, a reduced dimension of 15 achieves a relative error of around 10⁻³.
For the rough Bergomi model, a reduced dimension of 55 ensures machine precision.
The L2-error of the reduced system is very similar to the relative error in implied volatility.
Signatures for semi-martingales are defined using Stratonovich iterated integrals.
The rough path lift of a semi-martingale almost surely takes values in the space of geometric α-Hölder rough paths for 1/3 < α < 1/2.
The solution map of a rough differential equation is locally Lipschitz continuous.
The shuffle product allows the product of signature functionals to be expressed as a linear functional of the signature.
Time-extended paths (with running time as a component) ensure unique determination of the path by its signature.
The truncated tensor algebra Tm(V) is equipped with the standard Euclidean metric.
The signature formally solves a controlled ODE on the extended tensor algebra.
The truncated signature satisfies a similar ODE on the truncated tensor algebra.
The universal approximation property of signatures is proven using the Stone-Weierstrass theorem.
